title: WM-MT142-MergeEngine
clause: source_control merge engine: merge_branch with typed MergeOutcome, ff detection, no-ff 3-way, abort, no force flags

scope.summary:
GOAL: Close the verified merge gap in handshake_core source control. The current SourceControlRepository (src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control.rs) exposes status/diff/stage/unstage/discard/commit/log/branches/create_branch/switch_branch/blame (~lines 154-365) and NOTHING for merge/rebase/cherry-pick/pull ('Unmerged' appears only as a git-status code). This MT adds a governed merge engine as a NEW module so session branches (MT-141) can merge back into target branches with typed outcomes, an always-available abort, and provable absence of force flags and push.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge.rs (registered in lib.rs) containing the typed merge API; NO behavioral edits to existing source_control.rs functions (only pub(crate) visibility relaxation of small helpers like literal_pathspec/validate_branch_name if reuse requires it). New tests in src/backend/handshake_core/tests/. The new module is the ONLY place merge command lines are constructed, which makes the no-force/no-push grep proof precise (existing `clean -f` in discard() and `worktree remove --force` in workspace_safety.rs are pre-existing, non-merge, non-push code and stay untouched).

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Typed API:
   pub struct MergeOptions { pub allow_fast_forward: bool, pub commit_message: Option<String>, pub attribution: Option<String> }  // attribution = session/role identity folded into the merge commit message trailer
   pub struct MergeConflictStages { pub base_oid: Option<String>, pub local_oid: Option<String>, pub remote_oid: Option<String> }  // stages 1/2/3 from `git ls-files -u -z`; None = side absent (add/add, delete/modify)
   pub struct MergeConflict { pub path: String, pub stages: MergeConflictStages }
   pub enum MergeBlockReason { DirtyTargetTree { paths: Vec<String> }, DirtySourceTree { paths: Vec<String> }, MergeAlreadyInProgress, UnknownRef { name: String }, TargetProtectedApprovalRequired { target: String } }
   pub enum MergeOutcome { CleanMerged { commit_id: String, fast_forward: bool }, Conflicts { conflicts: Vec<MergeConflict>, checkout_path: PathBuf }, Blocked { reason: MergeBlockReason } }
   pub struct MergeSession { /* owns the controlled target checkout */ }
   impl MergeSession {
     pub fn begin(repo_root: &Path, target_branch: &str, source_branch: &str, opts: &MergeOptions) -> Result<MergeOutcome, SourceControlError>
     pub fn abort(&self) -> Result<(), SourceControlError>          // always available while Conflicts state persists
     pub fn checkout_path(&self) -> &Path
   }
2. Git command lines (every invocation: `git -C <cwd> -c core.longpaths=true ...`; worktree-creating/removing calls serialized under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK, imported from workspace_safety):
   ref validation:        `git check-ref-format --branch <name>` (reuse validate_branch_name pattern, source_control.rs ~336-350)
   ff detection:          `git merge-base --is-ancestor <target_commit> <source_commit>`  (exit 0 => source is ahead => ff possible)
   controlled checkout:   `git -C <repo_root> -c core.longpaths=true worktree add <merge_scratch_path> <target_branch>`  // named-branch checkout of TARGET in an external scratch path (under HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_ROOT sibling dir merge_checkouts/<uuid_v7>); NEVER merges inside the operator's live worktree
   ff merge (allowed):    `git -C <checkout> -c core.longpaths=true merge --ff-only <source_branch>`
   3-way merge:           `git -C <checkout> -c core.longpaths=true merge --no-ff --no-commit <source_branch>`
   conflict enumeration:  `git -C <checkout> -c core.longpaths=true ls-files -u -z`  -> parse (mode, oid, stage, path) rows into MergeConflict list
   abort:                 `git -C <checkout> -c core.longpaths=true merge --abort`
   completion commit:     `git -C <checkout> -c core.longpaths=true commit --no-gpg-sign -m <message>` (same no-gpg-sign discipline as commit(), source_control.rs ~275)
3. Preconditions (evaluated inside begin(), before any merge command): target checkout clean and source worktree clean via `status --porcelain=v1 -z` (reuse status() parsing); .git/MERGE_HEAD absent in the checkout (else MergeAlreadyInProgress); both refs resolve. Dirty trees return MergeOutcome::Blocked, never a partial merge. TargetProtectedApprovalRequired is RETURNED here as a typed reason but the protected-branch policy/approval evaluation itself is MT-145 (this MT ships the enum arm + a policy hook trait `MergePolicyGate { fn check(&self, target: &str) -> Result<(), MergeBlockReason> }` with a default allow-all implementation; MT-145 supplies the real gate).
4. HARD RULES (operator + red-team): NO force flag of any kind in this module (--force, -f, -D, --force-with-lease); NO `git push` invocation at all (merge-back is local; publishing is a separate operator concern outside this WP); NO auto-resolution of conflicts (no `-X ours`, `-X theirs`, no `git checkout --ours/--theirs`): Conflicts always surface as MergeOutcome::Conflicts for the native merge UI / operator / governed resolution session (MT-143). Unresolved MergeSession Drop aborts the merge and removes the scratch checkout (never half-committed).
5. BOUNDARY: this engine merges git-tracked worktree CODE only. CRDT document merging (kernel/crdt live shared documents) is a different mechanism and MUST NOT be routed through, or conflated with, this engine.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read source_control.rs 96-450 (SourceControlRepository, SourceControlError, run_git_bytes, validate_branch_name, literal_pathspec, status parsing) and workspace_safety.rs SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK.
2. Create source_control_merge.rs with the types above; register `pub mod source_control_merge;` in lib.rs.
3. Implement precondition checks (clean trees, refs resolve, no MERGE_HEAD, policy hook).
4. Implement ff detection + --ff-only path (only when opts.allow_fast_forward).
5. Implement the scratch-checkout no-ff no-commit path, conflict enumeration via ls-files -u -z, and the Conflicts outcome carrying checkout_path for MT-143.
6. Implement completion commit (clean 3-way) with attribution trailer, abort(), and Drop = abort + scratch cleanup.
7. Add SourceControlError variants as needed (e.g. MergeFailed { stderr }).
8. Tests in a scratch git repo: clean ff, clean no-ff, conflict outcome with correct stage oids, abort restores pristine state, dirty-tree Blocked, unknown-ref Blocked, Drop-aborts.
9. Run proof targets including the no-force/no-push greps.
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control.rs (visibility-only edits: pub(crate) on reused helpers; no behavior change)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (GUI IPC allowed only on the GUI MT, MT-146)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/kernel/crdt/** (CRDT document merging is a separate domain; do not conflate with git worktree code merge)
acceptance_criteria: MergeOutcome { CleanMerged{commit_id, fast_forward}, Conflicts{conflicts, checkout_path}, Blocked{reason} } and MergeBlockReason exist as typed, serde-serializable enums in src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge.rs.

MergeSession::begin performs ff detection via `merge-base --is-ancestor` and, for 3-way, runs `merge --no-ff --no-commit` in a controlled scratch worktree checkout of the TARGET branch, never in the operator's live worktree.
Conflicts are enumerated from `git ls-files -u -z` into MergeConflict rows with stage-1/2/3 oids; a live conflict test asserts path + all three stage oids.
MergeSession::abort runs `git merge --abort` and a test proves the checkout returns to pristine target state; Drop of an unresolved MergeSession aborts and removes the scratch checkout.
Dirty target tree, dirty source tree, in-progress merge, and unknown ref each return the matching typed Blocked reason without executing any merge command.
No auto-resolution: the module contains no -X ours/theirs and no checkout --ours/--theirs path; a conflict NEVER auto-commits.
Grep-provable hard rule: zero occurrences of '--force', '"-f"', '-D', 'push', '-X' in source_control_merge.rs.
Every git invocation in the module includes -c core.longpaths=true; worktree add/remove calls hold SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK.
MergePolicyGate hook exists with default allow-all; TargetProtectedApprovalRequired arm compiles and is reachable via an injected test gate (real policy lands in MT-145).
code_surfaces: src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge.rs (NEW: MergeOptions, MergeOutcome, MergeConflict, MergeBlockReason, MergeSession, MergePolicyGate)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control.rs (reused helpers: run_git_bytes pattern, validate_branch_name ~336, literal_pathspec, status parsing ~154-162; no behavior change)
expected_tests: scratch-repo test: ff merge returns CleanMerged{fast_forward:true} and target ref advances
scratch-repo test: divergent branches produce a no-ff merge commit with attribution trailer, CleanMerged{fast_forward:false}
scratch-repo test: overlapping edits return Conflicts with correct path and 3 stage oids matching `git rev-parse :1/:2/:3`
scratch-repo test: abort() then `git status --porcelain` empty in checkout; target ref unchanged
scratch-repo test: dirty target/source => Blocked{DirtyTargetTree|DirtySourceTree} and no MERGE_HEAD created
scratch-repo test: Drop of unresolved MergeSession leaves no scratch checkout directory and no MERGE_HEAD
unit test: injected MergePolicyGate returning TargetProtectedApprovalRequired blocks before any git merge command runs
implementation_notes: Scratch checkout root: sibling of the session worktree root (session_worktree_path pattern, workspace_safety.rs ~356-368) => merge_checkouts/<uuid> under HANDSHAKE_SESSION_WORKTREE_ROOT or <repo_parent>/merge_checkouts; ids minted with Uuid::now_v7() (HBR-INT-008).

The target branch cannot be checked out twice: if the target is already checked out in the main worktree, `git worktree add <path> <target_branch>` fails; detect and surface as a typed Blocked reason or use the main checkout ONLY when it is the operator-approved target checkout — decision recorded in code comment; default = dedicated scratch checkout of a non-checked-out target, and a typed error otherwise.
ls-files -u -z row format: '<mode> <oid> <stage>\t<path>' NUL-terminated; group rows by path into MergeConflictStages.
Do not implement rebase/cherry-pick/pull here; the verified gap this family closes is merge-back only.

Emit an EventLedger/FR record for merge attempt outcomes only via the MT-145 governance layer; this MT keeps the engine pure and returns typed outcomes (HBR-INT-001 evidence lands with MT-145 wiring; engine tests prove outcomes deterministically).
Cross-family seam: MT-123 MT-run states are merge preconditions read in MT-145, not here; keep the engine policy-agnostic behind MergePolicyGate.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless merge engine; operator-facing merge review UI is MT-146, conflict UI bridge is MT-143. Outcomes are typed and reconstructable (HBR-VIS-004).

target_entries: Source Control > Merging session branches (outcomes: clean / conflicts / blocked; abort always available)
Source Control > Merge safety rules (no force, no push, no auto-resolution, code-merge vs CRDT-document boundary)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Merge-lifecycle FR kinds (proposed/approved/executed/conflicted/aborted) are MT-161 seam, wired by MT-145; the engine stays event-free by design and this disposition must be recorded, not silently skipped.
Emit a diagnostic event when a merge git subprocess fails unexpectedly (non-conflict non-zero exit) if the open diagnostic-event API exists in the implementing worktree.
Bounded git subprocesses; no long-lived runtime whose freeze/crash needs external capture.

risk_if_missed: The verified surface gap stays open: no governed merge path exists, agents hand-roll git merges without typed outcomes/abort/no-force guarantees, and MT-143..148 have no engine to build on.

risks: RISK-1: A merge runs in the operator's live worktree instead of a controlled checkout, leaving conflict markers/MERGE_HEAD in the surface the operator is editing.
RISK-2: A 'convenient' auto-resolution strategy (-X theirs / checkout --ours) sneaks in and silently destroys one side of a conflict — the exact failure the no-auto-resolution hard rule forbids.
RISK-3: Force flags or a push path enter the module later; without a grep-provable module boundary the absence proof degrades into trust.

RISK-4: Half-committed state: a panic/early-return between `merge --no-commit` and commit/abort leaves MERGE_HEAD + staged conflict soup that blocks every later merge (MergeAlreadyInProgress forever).
RISK-5: Conflict stage parsing loses add/add or delete/modify cases (missing stages) and MT-143 renders the wrong base/local/remote panes.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): begin() always operates on a dedicated scratch checkout path derived under the external worktree root; a test asserts the repo's main worktree is byte-identical before/after a conflicted merge + abort.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): No -X/--strategy-option accepted anywhere in the API; grep proof target includes '-X'; conflict tests assert both sides' content still present in stage oids.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): All merge command construction confined to source_control_merge.rs; proof target greps that single module for --force/-f/-D/push/-X on every run (MT-148 re-proves it live).

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): MergeSession implements Drop = abort + scratch removal; test kills the session mid-conflict and proves no MERGE_HEAD survives; MergeAlreadyInProgress precondition covers external leftovers.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): ls-files -u parser has unit tests for add/add (no stage 1), delete/modify (missing stage 2 or 3), and rename-ish paths with spaces (NUL-terminated parsing).

research_provenance.source: Verified current code: wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1 src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control.rs — full surface status/diff/stage/unstage/discard/commit/log/branches/create_branch/switch_branch/blame at ~154-365 with NO merge/rebase/cherry-pick/pull ('Unmerged' only as a status code); commit --no-gpg-sign pattern ~275; validate_branch_name + check-ref-format ~336-350; discard() uses clean -f (pre-existing, non-merge). workspace_safety.rs SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK + core.longpaths discipline ~370-440. Field practice: merge --no-ff --no-commit + ls-files -u stage enumeration is the standard porcelain-scriptable conflict workflow (git-scm docs); libgit2/gitoxide in-process merge rejected to keep one git-CLI discipline consistent with the existing module.
corrections: Hard rules baked in from operator + red-team decisions: NEVER force-push (no push at all in this module); no auto-resolution of conflicts — conflicts always surface to the native merge UI/operator/governed resolution session; protected-branch gating is a typed Blocked arm here, enforced by MT-145.
Engine placed in a NEW module so the no-force/no-push grep proof is precise despite pre-existing clean -f / worktree remove --force elsewhere.
Git worktree CODE merge strictly separated from CRDT document merging (kernel/crdt); boundary stated in scope, forbidden_paths, and manual entries.
